newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on support.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Friday on institutional support and follow-up speculative short-covering, traders said.
The most active January 1996 contract ended at an intra-day high of 20,130 yuan ($2,423) per tonne, rising 90 yuan. It opened at a low of 19,800.

September rose 110 to 21,120 yuan, October 100 to 20,700, November 110 to 20,450, December 150 to 20,200, the February 50 to 20,100 and March 110 to 20,160. April did not trade. May fell 530 to 19,950.
Combined volume fell to 58,540 tonnes from 85,580.
Copper opened down, but rebounded with most later-maturing contracts standing above the key 20,000-yuan support level despite ovenight losses on the London Metal Exchange.
Traders said that institutional support triggered large amounts of follow-up short-covering from retail speculators to push most contracts to close at their intra-day highs.
"Institutions successfully took advantage of the psychology of individuals to push prices above 20,000," one trader said.
"Many speculators were disappointed with few stop-loss orders emerging with LME's breaching $1,900 on Thursday, so they offset their short positions," he added.
Traders said few investors wanted to build short positions below 20,000 yuan with domestic spot copper prices around the 20,500 yuan level.
But Shanghai copper will not stand above 20,000 yuan if copper breaches the $1,800 level on the LME, they said.
"Fundamentals did not change at all despite today's rebound, copper will meet heavy hedge selling at high levels," a second trader said.
Analysts expected copper to test the key 20,000-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mixed. September fell 50 to 13,900 yuan, October unchanged at 14,000, November rose 200 to 14,150.
Combined volume fell to 1,150 tonnes from 1,340.
